  "text": "The first thing Nina repaired after retiring was a toaster that had never belonged to her.

Someone had left it beside the bins with a note: WORKS IF YOU HOLD THE LEVER.

She took it upstairs, replaced a spring, and returned it to the entrance hall with another note: NOW YOU DON’T HAVE TO.

By Friday, a desk lamp appeared outside her door.

Then a radio. Then a clock shaped like a pear.

Nina put up a sign: SMALL ELECTRICAL ITEMS ONLY. NO PRINTERS.

She had spent forty years fixing hospital equipment. Printers, she felt, could answer to someone else.

Most people left their names. The person who brought the blue fan left three oranges instead.

In July, the repairs stopped.

Nina assumed everyone’s things were working. She watered her plants. She took apart her own perfectly serviceable kettle and put it back together.

On the hottest afternoon of the year, there was a knock.

A girl from the fourth floor stood holding the blue fan.

“Again?” Nina asked.

“No. Mum says you probably need it more. Your windows face the sun.”

Behind the girl stood a small boy carrying an extension lead with both hands.

They installed the fan beside Nina’s chair. The boy insisted on testing all three speeds.

At the door, the girl paused.

“Have you got anything broken?”

Nina looked around the flat.

“The cupboard handle’s loose.”

“I can do screws,” the girl said.

Nina fetched her toolbox. Then she put three glasses on the kitchen table and cut the last orange into wedges."
